transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Meridian Head of Security), Marcus Reed (Meridian Risk Analyst), Priya Shah (Meridian Legal)

Optional auto sections:
Topics: SIG questionnaire walkthrough, SOC 2 evidence mapping, KMS/encryption, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, next steps
Action items: see metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery, AE at Redwood. With me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How are y'all doing?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready to get through the SIG. We've got Marcus and Priya on for evidence and legal checks.
[00:15] Marcus Reed: Hey all. Quick ask up front — we need to confirm if Redwood holds customer data at rest in your tenancy or if it's fully isolated in our VPC.
[00:25] Samir Patel: Good question. For hosted Redwood API, data is processed in our multi-tenant service, but we have options — Dedicated pools and Private (VPC) deployments where the control plane is isolated. Sorry, sometimes product names get messy in the transcript, but basically full private deployment is possible.
[00:40] Priya Shah: And for legal, do you provide a SOC 2 Type II report and do you allow limited scope redactions? We need to review the report before procurement sign-off.
[00:50] Avery Chen: Yes, we can share our SOC 2 Type II. We'll share the link and the mapping to SIG controls — that's part of the next steps. We'll also provide the CAIQ/SIG spreadsheet with evidence pointers.
[01:02] Lena Ortiz: Great. Let's jump into the SIG, starting with identity and access management.
[01:10] Samir Patel: Sure. For SSO, we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. We have SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based in the console with custom roles; audit logs capture role changes. Side note, some docs may say "Redwood console" or "Redwood console app" interchangeably — apologies if labels change.
[01:30] Marcus Reed: How granular are the RBAC policies? Can we limit token creation to specific teams?
[01:36] Samir Patel: Yes — you can scope API keys to projects and generate scoped tokens. For Dedicated/Private customers we can integrate with your IdP and sync group mappings via SCIM so token issuance is controlled by your IdP groups.
[01:50] Lena Ortiz: And where are the audit logs stored and for how long? Our retention policy is 1 year for security events by default.
[01:58] Samir Patel: By default audit logs are retained 90 days in hosted, but for Dedicated and Private we support configurable retention and can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3 push. We'll note exact retention options in the evidence doc.
[02:12] Priya Shah: Encryption — at rest and in transit? KMS integration? Who holds the keys?
[02:18] Avery Chen: All data in-transit uses TLS. At rest we use AES-256. For hosted customers we manage keys in our KMS; we also support customer-managed keys (CMK) via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Samir, do you want to add specifics?
[02:32] Samir Patel: Yeah, we can do AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-hsm in some private deployments. When customers request CMK, the encryption-at-rest keywrap is done with your CMK and audit records show KMS operations. There is occasional confusion in the SIG where folks ask for HSM attestation — we have guidance for that.
[02:50] Marcus Reed: If we use CMK, can Redwood or any of your engineers access plaintext?
[02:56] Samir Patel: No, with proper CMK setup we don't have the ability to decrypt without your key. For hosted we do manage keys but access controls and separation of duties apply; we include that in the SOC 2 controls mapping.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: Data residency — we need to ensure data for EU customers stays within EU regions.
[03:16] Avery Chen: We support region pinning. For hosted customers we can route requests to EU regions; for Private it's deployed in your chosen region or on-prem. We'll include a region map and proof of deployment in the evidence folder.
[03:30] Priya Shah: On the questionnaire, there are a few questions around vulnerability management and pen tests. Do you have third-party pen test reports and a cadence for vuln scans?
[03:38] Samir Patel: Yes — we do annual third-party penetration tests and quarterly internal scans. We also have a bug bounty program. We'll point to the summary report in the evidence zip; raw reports can be shared under NDA.
[03:50] Marcus Reed: Good. For audit logs, can we get immutable logs or are they editable? We need tamper-evident controls.
[03:58] Samir Patel: Logs are append-only; for Dedicated/Private we provide write-once retention strategies and S3 object lock can be used for immutability. We'll document that.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: Network controls — do you support private link or peering into our VPC?
[04:18] Avery Chen: Yes — Private offers VPC peering and private endpoints (private link equivalents) plus optional on-prem appliance in some cases. We'll share network topo diagrams.
[04:28] Priya Shah: For the SIG spreadsheet, we asked for evidence IDs next to each control — can you map the SOC 2 sections to SIG questions?
[04:36] Avery Chen: Absolutely. We'll deliver a mapping spreadsheet where SOC 2 sections (CC1-CC8) are linked to SIG controls and direct evidence files. That's part of the next steps.
[04:46] Marcus Reed: There's a question on vendor sub-processors. Who are your cloud providers and do you have a sub-processor register?
[04:52] Samir Patel: Primary infra is AWS, with GCP for some regions. We use Postgres providers and Vault for secrets management. We maintain a sub-processor list and will include it in the evidence bundle.
[05:02] Lena Ortiz: Incident response — can you walk through your IR playbook and SLA for breach notification?
[05:08] Samir Patel: We have an IR plan, avg detection/ttr metrics in our SOC reports, and a contractual notification window — typically 72 hours for material incidents. We'll provide the IR summary doc and contact process.
[05:18] Priya Shah: Legal question — data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses for EU — are those available?
[05:24] Avery Chen: Yes, DPA and SCCs are standard for EU customers; we can provide red-lined versions if needed as part of procurement.
[05:30] Lena Ortiz: A few SIG items seem ambiguous: one around key rotation frequency and another about key custody in multi-tenant hosted. Can you confirm rotation cadence and separation of duties?
[05:40] Samir Patel: Key rotation: default rotation is 90 days for service keys; customer CMKs follow your KMS policy. Separation of duties: we have role separation for key management with audit trails; those controls are enumerated in SOC 2.
[05:52] Marcus Reed: Another ask: can we run an on-prem POC to validate latency and log forwarding? We're leaning Dedicated/Private but want to bench it.
[05:59] Avery Chen: Yes — we typically do a pilot for customers wanting Dedicated. We'll scope a POC — sample throughput targets, latency SLOs, and log forwarding tests. Samir, we should capture POC checklist.
[06:10] Samir Patel: I'll capture an initial POC checklist: infra footprint, dataset sizing, throughput targets, KV cache behavior, quantization profile suggestions. We'll also run a small benchmark and provide results.
[06:26] Priya Shah: Will you require an NDA to share some of the raw reports?
[06:30] Avery Chen: For full raw pen-test or some compliance evidence yes, we usually share under an NDA. We'll include a link to the redaction policy.

[06:42] (Several minutes of screen-share where Samir walks through SIG spreadsheet — transcript gaps due to screen audio)

[20:15] Samir Patel: (screen share) On row 14 this maps to encryption controls, evidence file "encryption-evidence-2025.zip" — that file includes KMS diagrams and key custody statements. Note: some names may be slightly off in the exported file name.
[20:36] Lena Ortiz: I see the file. Can you confirm the specific artifact that shows audit log retention is configurable per tenant?
[20:42] Samir Patel: Yes — artifact "audit-retention-config.md" in the Dedicated folder shows retention settings and S3 export config.
[21:01] Marcus Reed: A minor point — the SIG asks about privileged access reviews. What cadence do you run those?
[21:08] Samir Patel: Quarterly privileged access reviews, tracked in our IAM system and evidenced by reports we can export.
[21:20] Priya Shah: On legal maintainability, we might request a tailored DPA clause around subcontractor notifications. Do you have a process for that?
[21:26] Avery Chen: Yes, we can negotiate limited changes for enterprise customers. We'll surface that to legal.

[29:00] Lena Ortiz: Could you confirm if audit logs include request/response bodies or just metadata? For PCI/PHI implications we need to avoid logging PII.
[29:08] Samir Patel: We do not log request/response bodies containing user prompt content by default for hosted; we have redaction and prefix-only caching. For Dedicated/Private you can configure whether full request bodies are logged and where they are sent. We'll include the logging policy doc.
[29:30] Marcus Reed: And where is the key for encrypted KV cache stored in private deployments?
[29:36] Samir Patel: In Private deployments we recommend a customer KMS or HSM. The local KV cache key can be wrapped with your CMK.

[35:10] (some cross-talk, clarifications, filler words)

[40:05] Avery Chen: Quick recap before we close — we'll send the completed SIG spreadsheet with evidence pointers, SOC 2 report link, sub-processor list, sample network topology, and POC checklist. We'll also schedule the KMS deep-dive and the Dedicated POC scoping call.
[40:20] Lena Ortiz: That sounds right. Marcus, Priya — anything else?
[40:24] Marcus Reed: No, just want timestamps for evidence delivery.
[40:27] Priya Shah: Please include legal contact for DPA review.
[40:30] Lena Ortiz: Also please include a statement about breach notification SLA in writing.
[40:34] Avery Chen: Will do — action items captured. We'll aim to have the evidence bundle and SOC 2 link by 2026-04-09.
[40:42] Samir Patel: I'll follow up with the network/topology PDF and the audit retention options doc.
[40:47] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll send calendar invites for the KMS deep-dive and POC scoping.
[40:52] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, bye.
[40:54] Marcus Reed: Bye.
[40:56] Priya Shah: Bye.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabeling of product names ("redwood dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), some screen-share sections have sparse timestamps.
